evidence.note: Claim: a generic ratchet over git ls-files reading [quality].max_file_bytes catches a new oversized file and a grown baselined file. Falsifier: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py::test_an_oversized_new_file_fails_the_ratchet fails to flag a temp 30010-byte file. Ran: pytest tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py -> errored first (no Config.quality), then 6 passed after wiring.
r-small-files, r-everything-configurable (limit is the knob), r-reuse-core (G.files reused), r-tell-dont-discover (note names the split action and the list)

chunk_findings.detail: `violations` treats an empty `oversized` result as proof that no Python file is over the limit, but `oversized` returns `{}` whenever the check is disabled (`limit <= 0`) or when git could not list files. Given the repository baseline is present and `violations(repo, 0)` is called, `over` is `{}` while `base` still contains the baseline entries, so the `set(base) - set(over)` loop appends “... is no longer over 0 bytes: delete its line ...” for every baselined file. Thus setting `[quality].max_file_bytes` to 0 (the documented off value) makes the ratchet fail, and a git-listing failure produces false baseline-stale violations instead of no result or a distinct error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:63 (`violations`)

chunk_findings.detail: The stated conformance requires per-area constants that mean the same thing as `[quality].max_file_bytes` to be replaced, but the manifest for this change contains no edit to `tests/test_config_layout.py` (or the other layout tests) where `MAX_MODULE_CHARS = 30000` still exists. With an org lock such as `[quality].max_file_bytes = 20000`, the new ratchet rejects a 25000-byte module, while `test_config_layout.py` still permits up to 30000 characters, leaving a hardcoded duplicate cap and violating [r-everything-configurable]/[r-small-files]. The added architecture note only excuses `MAX_*_LINES` caps, not the character cap.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_config_layout.py:MAX_MODULE_CHARS

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline is explicitly declared shrink-only and says “never add a line,” but this line adds an exemption for `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` whose own reason says the file “crossed the limit after the baseline was first measured.” That is a newly oversized file being grandfathered. Given `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` at 30393 bytes and `[quality].max_file_bytes` 30000, `FS.violations` should report a new oversized file; because the baseline line exists, `test_no_new_oversized_file_and_no_baselined_file_grew` passes instead, violating the intent’s “fails a new oversized file” and “baseline … only shrinks.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/file_size_baseline.txt:18

chunk_findings.detail: The intent requires `[quality].max_file_bytes` to be added with “org lock”, but the `knob(...)` definition passes only `doc` and `check`. It does not declare `lock`/`org_lock` or an equivalent org-policy lock property, so the knob is not registered as org-lockable. An organization setting this limit in shared org config could have a local clone override it (for example `max_file_bytes = 0` to turn the check off), defeating the `r-small-files` ratchet the change is meant to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/quality.py:QualityConfig.max_file_bytes

chunk_findings.detail: `violations` does not honor the “check is off” case that `oversized` explicitly implements for `limit <= 0`. Given a repo with the non-empty default baseline and `[quality].max_file_bytes = 0`, `oversized` returns `{}`, but `violations` still reads the baseline and loops over `set(base) - set(over)`, appending “is no longer over 0 bytes: delete its line” for every baseline entry. The ratchet would then fail even though the limit knob is set to disable the check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:violations

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline has 14 exempt entries, not the 11 stated in the intent. The last entry exempts `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` at 30393 bytes and its own reason says it “crossed the limit after the baseline was first measured.” That is a newly over-limit source file added to the shrink-only baseline, so `FS.violations(ROOT, LIMIT)` will pass the current repo even though a source file exceeds `[quality].max_file_bytes`. This defeats the new-file ratchet and violates the file’s own header “never add a line.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/file_size_baseline.txt:18

chunk_findings.detail: `LIMIT` is captured once from `Config().quality.max_file_bytes`, and `test_default_limit_is_30k` hardcodes 30000. In a supported org-locked configuration that sets `[quality].max_file_bytes` to a non-default value such as 40000, importing the test makes `LIMIT = 40000` and the assertion `LIMIT == 30000` fails; the remaining ratchet tests then use the wrong limit.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:15,19

chunk_findings.detail: The new `limit <= 0` guard only suppresses the explicitly disabled-limit case; `violations` still treats an empty `oversized` result as proof that no Python file is over the limit. When `oversized` returns `{}` because `git ls-files` cannot list files (git unavailable, missing/inaccessible `.git`, permission failure, etc.), `base` still contains the repository baseline, so `set(base) - set(over)` yields every baseline path and the function returns false “no longer over limit: delete its line” violations for all baselined files. The added test only exercises `FS.violations(repo, 0)`, so the previously reported false-stale behavior for a failed git scan remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:violations

chunk_findings.detail: The org-lock fix is incomplete: `LIMIT` is still captured from `Config().quality.max_file_bytes`, and the ratchet tests still run against the single repository baseline using that configured limit. If an org-locked config sets `[quality].max_file_bytes` to a valid higher value such as `40000`, baselined files like `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` at `30393` bytes are no longer returned by `oversized(ROOT, 40000)`, so the stale-baseline loop reports them and `test_no_new_oversized_file_and_no_baselined_file_grew` fails even though no baselined file grew. Changing `test_default_limit_is_30k` to assert `QualityConfig().max_file_bytes` only fixes the default-value assertion, not the org-locked ratchet behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:LIMIT

chunk_findings.detail: The added `limit <= 0` guard only fixes the disabled-limit branch from the earlier finding. The other branch remains: `oversized` still returns `{}` when git cannot list files, and `violations` still treats an empty `over` as proof that every baselined file is stale. With a non-empty baseline and a git-listing failure, `violations(repo, 30000)` appends a “delete its line” violation for each baseline entry even though those files are still oversized; with an empty baseline it returns `[]` and misses a new oversized file. The new test exercises only `limit 0`, not the git-failure path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:violations

chunk_findings.detail: `MAX_MODULE_BYTES` is now read from `Config().quality.max_file_bytes`, and `test_each_config_submodule_is_small` enforces `size <= MAX_MODULE_BYTES` unconditionally. But the same change codifies `limit <= 0` as “the check is off” in `file_size.violations`, and the new test validates that with `max_file_bytes = 0`. In a configuration with `[quality].max_file_bytes = 0`, every non-empty config submodule fails this test, so the knob being “off” makes this layout test fail instead of disabling the size check.

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest contains no modification to the existing layout tests named in the intent, so the stated `MAX_MODULE_CHARS = 30000` constant remains after this change. That leaves two independent size limits in the repository: the new `[quality].max_file_bytes` knob and the old hard-coded constant. For example, with an org shared config setting `[quality].max_file_bytes = 25000`, the new ratchet/doctor enforce 25000 bytes, but the unmodified layout test still permits a 28000-byte module because it compares against 30000, violating the conformance requirement that the limit be the knob `[quality].max_file_bytes` and not a constant [r-small-files].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_config_layout.py

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest states that this change contains only 8 files, and none of them are the existing layout tests such as `tests/test_config_layout.py`. Therefore the old hard-coded `MAX_MODULE_CHARS = 30000` remains in place. The stated intent and conformance requirement are that `[quality].max_file_bytes` replace per-area constants where they express the same limit; `MAX_MODULE_CHARS` is a module-size cap, so after this change there are still two independent limits. For example, if an org lock sets `max_file_bytes` to a different value, the old layout test still enforces 30000 characters independently, and the generic ratchet has not replaced that per-area check.
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_config_layout.py:MAX_MODULE_CHARS` [r-everything-configurable]

chunk_findings.detail: `oversized` returns `{}` when `G.files(...)` yields no entries/None, and the docstring explicitly says that includes the case where “git could not list the files”. Both `violations` and `doctor_notes` then treat that as “no oversized files”, so the guard is silently disabled if the repository is not a git repo or git listing fails. For example, copying a repository containing a 40000-byte `huge.py` to a directory without `.git` makes `violations(Path(dir), 30000)` return `[]` and `doctor_notes` return `[]`, so a new oversized file passes the ratchet and doctor reports nothing. A quality guard should fail closed or report that git listing failed, not silently pass.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/file_size.py:oversized`

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline is declared shrink-only and is supposed to fail a new oversized file, but this line adds an exemption for `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` and its own reason states that the file “crossed the limit after the baseline was first measured.” That means it was not one of the originally baselined over-limit files; adding it now makes the new ratchet treat a newly oversized file as exempt. With `[quality].max_file_bytes` at 30000, a repo state where `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` is 30393 bytes passes the ratchet because it is listed, whereas the intended guard behavior is to fail such a file until it is split. This also makes the baseline 14 entries, beyond the 13 entries acknowledged in the recorded FINDING.
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/file_size_baseline.txt:18

chunk_findings.detail: The module captures the live configured value with `LIMIT = Config().quality.max_file_bytes` and then asserts `LIMIT == 30000`. The stated conformance says the limit is the `[quality].max_file_bytes` knob and that org policy can lock that knob; the tests themselves also treat `0` as a valid value that turns the ratchet off. If an org policy locks the knob to `0`, `test_default_limit_is_30k` fails immediately because `0 != 30000`. Worse, `test_an_oversized_new_file_fails_the_ratchet` then executes `[msg] = FS.violations(repo, LIMIT)` with `LIMIT == 0`; since the same file asserts that `FS.violations(repo, 0) == []`, the unpacking raises `ValueError` instead of producing the expected violation message. The test should test the schema default or patch/fixture the knob rather than depend on the live org-locked config. [r-everything-configurable]
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:12

chunk_findings.detail: A commit that adds a new oversized `.py` file and also adds a matching baseline line for it (e.g. `new_file.py | 40000 | reason`) makes `violations()` return no error for that file, because line 61 only treats `rel not in base` as a “new” oversized file. The intent says the ratchet must fail a new over-limit file and the baseline lists today’s exceptions and “only shrinks”; this implementation accumulates exemptions without any way to distinguish an added baseline entry from a pre-existing one, so a new oversized file can pass the guard simply by adding its own baseline line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/file_size.py:61

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline’s own header says it is shrink-only and to “never add a line or raise a size,” and the intended ratchet must fail a new oversized file. Yet line 14 adds `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py | 30393 | ... crossed the limit after the baseline was first measured ...`. That entry makes the ratchet accept a newly oversized source file instead of failing it, contrary to [r-small-files] and the change’s stated behavior. Given a commit where `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py` is 30,393 bytes and is not already baselined, the test will treat it as exempt and pass. The file should be reduced below `[quality].max_file_bytes` or fixed, not listed in the shrink-only baseline.
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/file_size_baseline.txt:14

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture creates a fresh git repo and writes `big.py`, but it never stages the file (`git add big.py`). The ratchet is specified to run over `git ls-files`, and in a newly initialized repo `git ls-files` returns no entries. Therefore `FS.violations(repo, LIMIT)` in `test_an_oversized_new_file_fails_the_ratchet` returns `[]`, the `[msg] = ...` unpacking raises `ValueError`, and the other tmp-repo tests that expect a violation also fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper `_repo` runs `git init -q` in `tmp_path`, but never configures a local git user name and email (`git config user.name` and `git config user.email`). In isolated test environments (such as CI runners where global git config is absent), any subsequent git operation that attempts to commit or inspect git state can fail, leading to flaky test failures.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:53

The change explicitly supports disabling the ratchet with `limit <= 0` (`oversized`/`violations` return `[]` for `0`, and `test_limit_zero_turns_the_ratchet_off_even_with_a_baseline` asserts that). If an org config or local config sets `[quality].max_file_bytes = 0`, then `LIMIT == 0`, so `FS.violations(tmp_path, LIMIT)` returns `[]` before attempting any git listing, but the test expects `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="cannot measure")`. Thus the test suite fails under a supported configuration that turns the knob off; the test should use a positive fixed limit or skip/adjust when `LIMIT <= 0`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:test_a_listing_git_cannot_give_is_an_error_not_an_empty_result

chunk_findings.detail: The new test uses the module-level `LIMIT`, which is captured from `Config().quality.max_file_bytes` and therefore depends on configuration. With a supported org-locked `[quality].max_file_bytes = 0` (the code explicitly treats `<= 0` as “the check is off,” and `tests/test_config_layout.py` now accommodates `MAX_MODULE_BYTES == 0`), `LIMIT` is `0`. Then `FS.violations(tmp_path, 0)` returns `[]` via the existing `limit <= 0` guard before `_listed`/`oversized` ever attempts to invoke git, so no `RuntimeError` is raised and `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="cannot measure")` fails with `DID NOT RAISE`. Thus a valid configuration breaks the repository’s own test suite.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_file_size_ratchet.py:test_a_listing_git_cannot_give_is_an_error_not_an_empty_result

chunk_findings.detail: `test_each_config_submodule_is_small` checks `MAX_MODULE_BYTES == 0 or size <= MAX_MODULE_BYTES`. However, the global file-size ratchet permits the check to be turned off with `limit <= 0` (where `limit` can be negative, e.g., `-1`). When `[quality].max_file_bytes` is set to `-1`, `MAX_MODULE_BYTES` becomes `-1`. The test condition `MAX_MODULE_BYTES == 0` evaluates to `False`, and `size <= -1` fails for any non-empty config submodule (which has a positive size), causing layout tests to fail incorrectly when the check is disabled via negative limit values.
